recognize_zh: 一顆中央的嗜中性球被約八顆紅血球呈花瓣狀緊密環繞（rosette），這種排列在其他白血球周圍並不存在，屬於紅血球玫瑰花結現象。
features: Single central neutrophil with a band-to-bilobed, coarsely clumped nucleus
Pale cytoplasm with fine neutrophilic granules
About eight red cells arranged radially and tightly apposed to the neutrophil membrane, forming a rosette
Adherent red cells appear deformed/flattened against the leukocyte surface
Photographed from a monitor screen (cursor visible); fine detail is limited
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear (photographed from a display screen) shows a neutrophil encircled by a ring of approximately eight erythrocytes adhering to its surface in a rosette configuration. The neutrophil itself shows a band/bilobed nucleus with clumped chromatin and fine cytoplasmic granules, without evident phagocytosed material. No platelet satellitism is seen in this field. In the clinical setting of hypergammaglobulinemia, findings are consistent with red cell rosetting around a neutrophil, likely immunoglobulin-mediated and possibly an in vitro phenomenon.

ddx.vs: Satellitism shows platelets, not intact red cells, ringing the neutrophil and is EDTA-induced with pseudothrombocytopenia.
In erythrophagocytosis the red cells are engulfed within the neutrophil or macrophage cytoplasm rather than attached around its periphery.
LE cells contain a large homogeneous phagocytosed nuclear body within the cytoplasm, which is absent here.
Rouleaux are stacked linear chains of red cells in the background rather than a radial ring around a single leukocyte.
